Sandpapergate live: Bancroft outfit raises eyebrows, Piers Morgan declares Cummins ‘caught lying’

The pressure is continuing to build on Pat Cummins and Cricket Australia as the team’s Sandpapergate crisis heads into another day of drama.

Cameron Bancroft rocked the foundations of Cummins’ captaincy when he singled out the Aussie Test skipper in his explosive 4000-word tell-all article in The West Australian published on Wednesday night.

Never miss the latest sports news from Australia and around the world — download the news.com.au app direct to your phone.

Cummins responded through his manager after Bancroft dropped several bombshell claims, including that players gathered for a morning meeting on Day 3 of the Port Elizabeth Test where his use of sandpaper was “discussed and acknowledged” by the entire group.

Ex captain Steve Smith and former coach Darren Lehmann are now the next key figures the world is waiting to hear from.

Bancroft’s column has poured fuel on the burning criticism towards CA officials after CEO Todd Greenberg said a new investigation will not be launched after saying he was comfortable with how the 2018 investigation was carried out.

CA is instead preparing to put together an independent “forum” for players and staff involved in the Sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events in a “safe space”.

Nov 19, 2026
PINNED
HIGHLIGHT

Bancroft speaks, outfit detail raises eyebrows

Matthew Sullivan

After dropping his 4000-world bombshell, Cameron Bancroft spoke to media briefly today and one detail raised an eyebrow or two. The 33-year-old said he felt he had to break his silence on the sandpaper incident to be at “peace” with himself.

“Obviously yesterday was a really big day for me, really emotional day,” Bancroft said on Nine.

“I’ve been carrying a lot of this stuff for a long period of time. I feel really freed and really happy to be able to do that and obviously now there’s a process in place which Cricket Australia put (in place) and I look forward to being a part of that process.”

news.com.au
Cam Bancroft wears South Africa hat
Cameron Bancroft was wearing a Cape...

moreless

Toggle full description view
Source: News.com.au

“I never meant to point fingers or punish people or implicate people,” Bancroft said. “I just wanted to, for my own peace, to tell the truth. “This has been a burden that I’ve carried with me for such a long period of time. I feel very free and very happy that I’ve been able to do that.”

Eagle-eyed viewers noticed Bancroft was wearing a touristy cap from Cape Town’s V&A Waterfront shopping centre with the words “Cape Town, South Africa” written on it, along with a South African flag on the back.

Of course Bancroft was caught using sandpaper at Newlands, Cape Town in the third Test in South Africa in 2018.

So it was certainly an interesting wardrobe choice by him the day after he went public with revelations from that Test series.

“How good is the cap,” one person wrote on X, while another said: “The Cape Town hat has to be a p*ss take surely.”

4:47 AM
Nov 19, 2026
HIGHLIGHT

Michael Clarke fumes: 'I call bullshit'

Matthew Sullivan

Former Australian captain Michael Clarke says he’s had enough of Cricket Australia’s stance about there being several different versions of the truth around sandpaper-gate as CA pledged to listen to various recollections of events at its forum.

“I think there is the truth. I call bullshit. I don’t think there’s two sides to the story. I think there is the truth,” Clarke said on his Beyond 23 podcast on Thursday.

“If it’s not done properly it will keep going. I’m not picking a side right now, I’m saying there is no double truth or mixed truth there. I don’t believe that. There is the truth.

“We aren’t sitting here because of the crime. The Australian public, the fans, all of us who love the game, we’re past the crime. It’s the behaviour post the crime. The lying. Someone is lying.

“I want to know the truth. The fans want to know the truth.

“The public don’t want any more bullshit.

“The public want the complete truth to allow us to move on. The forum. We’re going to do a forum. The forum is done now! Cam Bancroft just ended the forum.”

More ⌄
2:28 AM
Nov 19, 2026

Oscar Piastri weighs into sandpaper-gate

Matthew Sullivan

Even Aussie F1 star Oscar Piastri has been asked for his two cents about sandpaper-gate as he prepares for this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Piastri is a massive cricket fan who has worn Brett Lee’s ODI jersey into the paddock and has a famous photo standing next to Ricky Ponting as a child.

“It has obviously been an interesting couple of weeks, that is for sure with what has been unfolding,” Piastri said.

“I know quite a few of the guys involved personally, so it is not really a nice thing to see it being brought back up necessarily, but it is what it is.

“Obviously I’ve got no knowledge, and I remember when it happened eight years ago, but I think for everyone, especially the Australian cricket community and Australia as a country, the quicker it can be dealt with, whatever that looks like, the better.

“I know myself as a sports person that the noise around certainly is not going to be helpful, so the quicker it can be resolved and put behind us, the better for everyone.”

More ⌄
2:25 AM
Nov 19, 2026

Khawaja backs Bancroft

Matthew Sullivan

Usman Khawaja has backed Cameron Bancroft after his explosive article backed up Khawaja’s claims in his book that the whole team knew about sandpaper.

“I’m glad that he’s gone out and said what he said,” Khawaja said.

“I’ve always supported him as a friend. I’ve been talking to him the last couple of weeks, and I think this is the first time he finally feels like he can move on from this.”

8:21 PM
Nov 18, 2026
HIGHLIGHT

Two words to save Cummins

Tyson Otto

Everyone in cricket appears to be reaching the same conclusion – that two words can save Pat Cummins’ captaincy.

The fast-bowler – and all members of the Australian bowling cartel – still have plausible deniability despite the new accusations made by Usman Khawaja, David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Cameron Bancroft.

Former English Test captain Michael Vaughan said exactly that on Wednesday night after Bancroft’s article was published.

“There’s no way in a million years that a team wouldn’t know what’s going on,” Vaughan told the BBC.

“Now it’s plausible that on that given day in Cape Town, certain players, certain bowlers, didn’t know that there was sandpaper on the pitch at that given moment.

“It’s never sat pretty with me that only a few would have known that something was being used on that ball and it now seems it was (in) Port Elizabeth where it was first used.”

He noted that a lot of focus has been on the fateful day during the Cape Town Test and not the earlier Test in Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqebertha.

“Cape Town on that given day that we’re all talking about, it is plausible that a few bowlers didn’t know on that given day,” Vaughan said.

“But it doesn’t sit with me that they didn’t know in Port Elizabeth.”

Bancroft makes telling move after bombshell

Tyson Otto

Cameron Bancroft has indicated he will take part in the controversial independent forum Cricket Australia is establishing for any parties to share information about the Sandpapergate scandal.

Cricket Australia has been widely criticised for stopping well short of launching a new investigation despite new claims from Usman Khawaja, David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Bancroft.

After coming clean in an extraordinary 4000-word newspaper column, Bancroft on Thursday morning told 9News in Perth: “Obviously, yeah, I’ve been carrying a lot of this stuff for a long period of time.

“So I feel really freed and really happy to be able to do that. And obviously now there’s a process in place which Cricket Australia have put in (forum). Yeah, I look forward to being a part of that process.”

Cummins and wife put on public display

Tyson Otto

Pat Cummins has emerged to put on a public display with wife Becky.

The Aussie Test captain faced a barrage of media questions outside his Sydney home on Thursday morning.

Media Mode reports Cummins said he “feels for Cam”.

When asked whether he regretted the recent press conference, the skipper appeared to respond “Yeah”.

The 33-year-old was polite, but dismissive when telling the media pack outside his house he was “just off to training guys, thankyou”.

Photos showed Cummins and Becky kissing out the front of their home.

It has only been one week since Cummins and Becky had a public disagreement.

Cummins insisted during his 70-minute press conference that he was not having a spat with his partner and suggested Usman Khawaja’s autobiography was at the heart of the issue.

“Becky wears her heart on her sleeve,” he said.

“We weren’t having a spat, Becky was very frustrated and animated and really unhappy with Usman.”

'Deal with bullying': Bancroft's form never recovered

Tyler Lewis

Cameron Bancroft’s manager says the former Test opener has emerged a better person from the sandpaper scandal despite its lasting impact on his career.

Bancroft’s manager Ben Tippett from Entourage Sports told SEN the cricketer had to confront “bullying” during his career.

“No one can really understand what he’s gone through because it’s so intense on him,” Tippett told SEN.

“I remember just after it, talking to him, and his reflections on it, and a long time before this happened, and he really felt like it changed him for the better.

“You know, he became a better human and understanding of leadership and sometimes those big events really change you.

“There’s all those questions about how you deal with bullying, you know, being a junior member and speaking up for yourself, telling the truth.

“They’re all lessons he learned first hand in a pretty significant way. It’s certainly shaped him as a better person from all of that time.

“I guess as it’s come out, his cricket has been really affected by it, but he’s really strong-minded, has the ability to compartmentalise.

Sayers regrets not speaking out earlier

Tyson Otto

Retired fast bowler Chadd Sayers says he has regrets about not speaking up earlier after hearing Cameron Bancroft’s latest account.

Sayers said on Thursday he did not intend to ever speak publicly about his involvement in the Sandpapergate operation – but was unable to avoid the topic when it came up during an appearance on radio.

“I was pretty comfortable. Knowing what happened is not great, and knowing a lot of people were telling the truth and some weren’t, but I was pretty comfortable that it had moved on,” Sayers told SEN Breakfast.

He went on to say: “Now knowing what Cameron Bancroft actually had gone through and all the different scenarios that have happened, I probably wish I did come out a bit earlier.”
